findings.title: AST-layer 'every threshold' claim inaccurate for SHARED mode
findings.problem: README's Migration section states AST-layer sandbox-escape detections (exec/eval/__import__/__builtins__) are 'blocked at every threshold, including SAFE and LOW' - but the default SandboxMode.SHARED path (_validate_code_security, code_executor_tool.py:589) validates code via session.is_safe(), llm_sandbox's own regex-only check, and never calls check_security_policy/check_code_with_ast at all.
findings.impact: A reader (including a security reviewer) would believe __import__/exec/eval/__builtins__ bypass techniques are always caught regardless of threshold, but for the default sandbox mode none of the AST-layer detections run - a false sense of protection for the most commonly used mode.
findings.recommendation: Scope the claim to where it is actually true (the check_security_policy path used by JOBS mode), or state plainly that the AST layer does not run for the default SHARED sandbox mode.

findings.title: check_code_with_ast docstring still claims threshold enforcement
findings.problem: check_code_with_ast's docstring (line 138) still describes severity_threshold as 'Minimum severity level to enforce', but the parameter is only stored as self.threshold on the checker and never read - _add_violation's own docstring confirms it is 'no longer branched on'.
findings.impact: A maintainer reading only the public function's docstring would believe passing SAFE/LOW reduces AST-layer detection, when detection is identical at every threshold - exactly the documentation drift the ticket asked to correct.
findings.recommendation: Update check_code_with_ast's docstring to state severity_threshold is retained for signature continuity only and does not affect which violations are reported.

findings.title: SAFE threshold description self-contradicts on 'blocks nothing'
findings.problem: models.py's security_threshold Field description (and the matching README table / yaml header comment) states 'SAFE: enforcement disabled, blocks nothing' and then, in the very next sentence, states AST-layer sandbox-escape detections are 'blocked at every threshold' - including SAFE.
findings.impact: A reader who takes the 'blocks nothing' claim at face value for SAFE is misled about the actual (stricter) enforcement posture at that setting.
findings.recommendation: Reword the SAFE description to state it disables pattern/module-based enforcement but not the AST layer's hardcoded bypass-technique blocking, consistently across models.py, the yaml header, and README.

findings.title: get_restricted_module_names has no direct test coverage
findings.problem: get_restricted_module_names was changed in this diff to run severity_threshold through translate_security_threshold before filtering policy.restricted_modules, but no test in the repository calls this function directly (zero matches for get_restricted_module_names under tests/); existing args_schema tests hardcode a literal blocked_modules string instead of computing it.
findings.impact: If the translation call in this function were dropped or reverted, blocked_modules_str shown to the LLM agent via the tool's args_schema (code_executor_tool.py:254-257) would silently misreport what check_security_policy actually blocks, with no test catching the regression.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that calls get_restricted_module_names with a real threshold and asserts on its actual output (e.g. the HIGH-threshold list is a superset of the LOW-threshold list, matching what check_security_policy actually blocks).

findings.title: TestOsModulePolicy/TestPipModulePolicy not re-verified across thresholds
findings.problem: Spec Section 6 requires TestOsModulePolicy/TestPipModulePolicy be re-verified 'with explicit assertions, not assumptions' that HIGH-severity patterns still block at every threshold except SAFE under the new mapping. Both classes' _check helpers still call get_codemie_security_policy(severity_threshold=SecurityIssueSeverity.LOW) only (lines 246, 310, 327); no assertions were added for SAFE, MEDIUM, or HIGH inputs.
findings.impact: The existing LOW-input assertions happen to pass under both the old and new translation (LOW maps to internal HIGH cutoff, and os/pip patterns are HIGH severity), so these tests would not catch a broken or reverted translate_security_threshold for SAFE/MEDIUM/HIGH inputs - a required regression-coverage gap for two of the codebase's core security-pattern test suites.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize TestOsModulePolicy/TestPipModulePolicy's _check helper by threshold (or add sibling tests) asserting SAFE allows, and MEDIUM/HIGH block, the same os/pip patterns, per spec Section 6.
